tranche: KleinOS v0.1 — one sandboxed in-world computer
objective: A player uses one computer object to open a Tkinter desktop with Files, Terminal, and Editor backed by one persistent, restricted Linux Docker container.
workflow: Baseline -> Container -> Backend -> Desktop -> Integrate -> Verify -> Park

filesystem_budget.note: If a genuine technical necessity requires another file, explain before expanding the footprint. Never rename either game.py in this tranche.

architecture.trusted_layer: KleinBOTTLE game process -> computer_backend.py -> Docker CLI (argv only, shell=False)
architecture.untrusted_layer: One non-root, offline, resource-limited Linux container with a single persistent named volume mounted at /workspace.
architecture.interface: One Tkinter Toplevel computer window with 3 views; return to Play without changing Notebook tabs.
architecture.world: GameSession identifies one visible kind=terminal object. World object metadata never controls arbitrary Docker image, mounts, executable, or container identity.
architecture.storage: Files, Terminal, and Editor operate on the same container /workspace; never treat a local host path as a fallback.
architecture.later_not_now: JSON room import/publish via existing WorldBuilder validation and explicit user approval.

hard_constraints: One computer and one sandbox. Do not build a general virtual-machine manager, OS, plugin framework, shell emulator, or agent.
No host bind mounts, network access, Docker socket inside the container, privileged mode, host PID namespace, or broad Linux capabilities.
Use non-root container user, read-only root filesystem, writable named /workspace volume, small /tmp tmpfs, no-new-privileges, cap-drop ALL, and CPU/memory/PID limits.
All submitted commands execute in container. No host-shell fallback and no shell=True in Python subprocess calls.
Treat in-game world JSON and terminal commands as untrusted data; use fixed Docker runtime configuration; validate all file paths against /workspace within the container, including symlinks.
Cap output, enforce command timeouts (including container-side termination), and do not block Tkinter's event loop.
Never modify live world files from terminal. Room publishing is a later tranche, via trusted WorldBuilder import only.
Preserve phone, game engine behavior, saved worlds, and development sidecars; do not change world data during install.

Avoid the previous ProjectMapper indentation failure: stage modifications, validate syntax/AST on proposed files before writing, use literal indentation for Python replacements, and test after every step.
If Docker is unavailable, show a clear error; do not silently execute on the host.

tasks.name: Verify and back up baseline
start_conditions: Work from the user's current local _KleinBOTTLE directory, not an older filedump.
steps: Back up the working project.
Check Docker CLI/daemon availability; do not change system configuration automatically.
Run Python syntax checks and existing tests; record results and current modified files.
tasks.target_end_state: Known-good source snapshot and exact baseline test results, ready for Docker setup.
verification: python -m compileall -q src tests
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
constraints: No source edits in this task.
If baseline is broken, repair/stop before adding functionality.

tasks.name: Build isolated container
start_conditions: K0 baseline passes or known preexisting issues are explicitly documented.
Docker Desktop + WSL2 Linux containers are running.
steps: Create Dockerfile.kleinos using a small pinned Python/Linux base image, a non-root user, and /workspace.
Create one deterministic container and one persistent named volume; implement startup flags in trusted backend in K2 rather than introducing scripts.
Apply --network none, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, --pids-limit, --memory, --cpus, writable volume /workspace, bounded /tmp tmpfs.
Prove a file survives container stop/start and that host paths are not mounted.
tasks.target_end_state: A restricted container can execute Python and persist /workspace independently of the GUI.
verification: docker info
docker inspect <container> (confirm mounts/network/security/limits)
Write a test file in /workspace, restart container, read the same file
constraints: No privileged container, network, source tree mount, Docker socket, or host file bindings.
Read-only container root filesystem; only /workspace and limited /tmp writable.

tasks.name: Implement minimal computer backend
start_conditions: K1 container design and security flags are defined.
steps: Create src/computer_backend.py exposing start/status/execute/list/read/write/stop for ONE fixed container and volume.
Invoke Docker with subprocess argv arrays, shell=False. Use fixed image, container, volume names.
Execute one shell command at a time inside the container; make current working directory explicit and restricted to /workspace (cd may be backend-managed).
Implement list/read/write through container operations and canonical path checks, not by opening host files.
Enforce bounded output, per-command timeout with container-side process termination, and meaningful Docker-offline errors.
tasks.target_end_state: Python API can run commands and manipulate files in the one isolated workspace without the game UI.
verification: Run pwd, ls, python -c, mkdir and file read/write inside container.
Reject paths traversing outside /workspace or resolving through a symlink outside /workspace.
Simulate missing Docker and confirm no host execution.
Verify long-running commands terminate within the agreed timeout.
constraints: No generic Docker control API exposed to game objects.

tasks.name: Build one mini desktop
steps: Create src/surfaces/computer.py as a themed Tkinter Toplevel window.
Provide three views using basic ttk/tk primitives: Files (folders/list/open), Terminal (command/output), Editor (edit/save text).
Wire all three to the same backend and /workspace.
Run Docker interactions on workers; communicate results safely back to the Tk thread.
Provide Close/Return control; display timeouts and Docker errors without crashing.
tasks.target_end_state: Desktop can browse, edit and run commands, then close cleanly with persistent files.
verification: Create and edit a text file, then cat it from the terminal.
Create a folder via shell and see it in Files.
Close/reopen desktop and retain data.
GUI remains responsive during a slow operation.
constraints: No embedded browser, desktop environment, multiprocess app framework, or real interactive PTY.
One simple window, not a new app shell.

tasks.name: Connect one world object
steps: In src/game.py, detect a visible room object with kind=terminal when the player types 'use computer' (and optionally 'use <object name>').
Use the existing object lookup conventions and explicit ambiguity/error messages.
In src/surfaces/game.py, open the computer Toplevel on a recognized game action; do not change Notebook tabs.
Keep world object data separate from Docker runtime configuration; use fixed sandbox identifiers.
Update help text; add a terminal object manually through the existing Builder, without modifying shipped data/world.json.
tasks.target_end_state: Player uses a terminal object in a room, operates computer, closes it, and resumes same game session.
verification: use computer opens the desktop only when visible matching kind=terminal object exists.
No terminal here produces clear feedback.
Phone still answers and hangs up.
Room, inventory, and game transcript preserved after closing computer.
constraints: Do not change WorldBuilder schema, builder UI, or live world files unless a test proves necessary.
Do not rename src/game.py or src/surfaces/game.py here.
Do not reset world on computer open/close.

tasks.name: Regression and isolation checks
steps: Create tests/test_computer.py with backend and game-command tests, mocking Docker for unit tests.
Run a separate real-Docker integration smoke test only when Docker is available.
Confirm one volume persists, container network is disabled, there are no bind mounts, and hostile paths are rejected.
Run existing game, builder, phone tests and a GUI smoke test.
tasks.target_end_state: Functional and security claims have reproducible checks; previously working features still pass.
verification: python -m compileall -q src tests
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
Docker inspect and in-container smoke checks
Manual open/run/edit/close/reopen game workflow
constraints: Do not claim Docker is escape-proof.
No silent skipped tests; label Docker-unavailable cases explicitly.

tasks.name: Document, report, park
start_conditions: K5 checks pass or blockers are clearly recorded.
steps: Add brief usage and Docker prerequisites to existing README.md.
Report files changed, test commands/results, security boundaries and remaining risks.
Back up the working slice and park the tranche.
tasks.target_end_state: Verified, documented KleinOS v0.1, with no active scope expansion.
verification: Stop conditions below are either verified or explicitly blocked.
constraints: No room publishing, generated game worlds, AI coding agent, multiple computers, or OS redesign.

stop_conditions: One in-room computer object opens a real mini desktop.
Desktop has Files, Terminal, Editor using the same /workspace.
Commands run only in the offline Docker container; no host fallback.
Files persist through window close and container restart.
Host files unavailable through container mounts; path/traversal checks enforced.
Opening/closing does not reset current gameplay; telephone still works.
Syntax checks and all existing/new tests pass.
Builder reports results, documents, and parks.
out_of_scope_v0_2: Create world JSON in sandbox -> trusted WorldBuilder validate/preview -> explicit user approval -> import/save -> reload world. Never direct sandbox writes to live world.
